what: Self-scored quality of every MCP tool description in the estate, before and after the loop 31 rewrite, against the six dimensions Glama publishes.

scoring_method.note: These are this project's own scores from a documented, reproducible heuristic, not Glama's. It is calibrated against the one datapoint Glama gives us: on mcp-statement-of-account it reproduces the published minimum of 2.9 (license_status, 2.90 here) and scores the mean lower than Glama's 3.7, so it is harsher than the real grader.
scoring_method.server_definition_score: 0.6 * mean(tool scores) + 0.4 * min(tool scores), the formula on the Glama score page

signals.purpose_clarity: 3, +1 for a first sentence of 8 words or more, +1 for a description of 150 chars or more
signals.usage_guidelines: 2, +1.5 when it names a sibling tool, +1 for a when-to-use clause, +0.5 when it states a tier
signals.behavioral_transparency: 2, +1 for what it returns, +1 for what it refuses, +1 for a side effect or a cap
signals.parameter_semantics: 2, +1 when it names a parameter, +1 more at three parameters, +1 for a unit or scale convention
signals.conciseness_structure: 5 at 150-220 chars, 4 at 110-149, 3 below 110, 2 above the estate's 220-char contract ceiling
signals.contextual_completeness: 2, +1 for a tier, +1 for cross-server context, +1 when it both returns and disambiguates

constraints_obeyed.source: servers/*/test/contract.test.mjs MAX_DESCRIPTION, with OVER_LENGTH_BASELINE empty on all 31 servers
constraints_obeyed.imperative_rule: a tool taking path, url, out_path, out_dir, paths, dir or template_path must open with 'Call this tool' or 'Use this'
